deferred_origins.reason: Checked on 2026-08-27 and reported "fullname":"Cohere Labs" with "isVerified":false. Every other Hugging Face organization approved in this directory is verified, and this one is not, so nothing here establishes that it is Cohere's own org rather than a name anyone could take. Its research models are reachable through the approved cohere.com and docs.cohere.com origins in any case. Approving it needs evidence this batch does not have — a first-party statement from Cohere naming the org would be enough.
Authenticated dashboard. Not reachable as a public primary source, so nothing about it could be verified.

ambiguities.topic: Command and Aya are not one family
ambiguities.note: Cohere publishes the Command line of enterprise models and the Aya line of multilingual research models, and the research work is associated with Cohere Labs rather than being marketed alongside Command.
ambiguities.guidance: Use Cohere's own family label for each and do not merge them. Which internal group published a model is an attribute, not a separate creator, unless a source presents Cohere Labs as a distinct organization — in which case that is an organization mapping for a human, not an inference to make here.

ambiguities.topic: Command naming carries generation, size and date at once
ambiguities.note: Identifiers such as command-a, command-r, command-r-plus and command-a-03-2025 encode a line, a tier and a snapshot date in one string.
ambiguities.guidance: Take the dated identifier from the documentation as the release and record the dateless form as an alias. Do not derive a tier or a generation the source does not state.

ambiguities.note: Cohere's models are served through major cloud platforms as well as Cohere's own API, and those platforms publish their own model identifiers.
ambiguities.guidance: Record third-party serving as a separate serving-platform or deployment entity, and keep platform-specific identifiers on the deployment rather than on the release's canonical name. Availability on a platform is never evidence about who trained the model.
